tasks.short: Represent administrative services in meetings, handle requests and complaints, and coordinate agreed responses.

steps.what: Read incoming requests and complaints, identify urgency, and choose the responsible service.

loop.input: Request or complaint text and approved service directory.
loop.output: Suggested service, urgency, and supporting text excerpts.
loop.check: Validate service against the directory; manager checks urgency and sensitive cases.
loop.stop: One classification pass; missing facts or uncertain routing go to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Routing depends on varied free text; explicit form submissions use rules instead.

steps.what: Check service records, previous correspondence, and outstanding commitments.
Prepare the meeting brief with facts, unresolved questions, and proposed positions.

loop.input: Linked case evidence, meeting agenda, and approved service policy.
loop.output: Brief with cited facts, open questions, and clearly labelled response options.
loop.check: Require source references; manager verifies positions and removes unsupported statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; conflicting evidence remains an open question.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but correspondence needs concise interpretation.

steps.what: Represent the service, listen to concerns, and explain constraints during the meeting.
Agree remedies and commitments within delegated authority, escalating exceptions.
Write the meeting record, including decisions, owners, deadlines, and unresolved issues.

loop.input: Manager's meeting notes and explicitly agreed commitments.
loop.output: Draft decision record and action list.
loop.check: Trace each action to notes; manager confirms owners, deadlines, and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing commitments stay unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes need interpretation; structured action entries bypass the model.

steps.what: Send agreed actions and deadlines to internal service owners.
Check action status and chase overdue responses.

tasks.design: Configure case ownership, approved-action assignment, and reminders in the {HELPDESK} and {WORKFLOW}; link accessible evidence from the {EMAIL} and {DOCS} through deterministic lookups. Small bounded loops propose routing, meeting briefs, and decision records with source references. The manager approves commitments and records; approved internal follow-up runs automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence and commitments sit across correspondence, documents, and service records. Bespoke connections cost more than the perceived administrative saving.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort for connectors and templates. Bounded text processing can prepare drafts, while existing configuration handles ownership and reminders; no breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous complaints, incomplete records, and disputed commitments require judgement. Evidence access must respect GDPR, and commitments beyond delegation still require the appropriate budget or service authority.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, repair trust, negotiate practical concessions, and recognise when a technically correct answer will fail.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one recurring complaint cause for a service improvement.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence assembly and chasing, with more time for difficult conversations and recurring service problems. Decision rights remain within existing delegation; prioritising improvements requires an explicit mandate.

reach.task: Prepare decision briefs and coordinate meeting follow-up.
reach.learn: Agenda design, concise decision writing, and escalation protocols.

reach.task: Analyse recurring complaints and propose process changes.
reach.learn: Cause analysis, comparable service measures, and small improvement experiments.

evidence.claim: Case linking, action assignment, and reminders can use deterministic integrations and existing configuration.
Bounded drafting can support preparation, but this digest supplies no directly matched case proving savings for this task.
Relationship handling and negotiated commitments remain human work.

assumptions: The manager handles both routine internal requests and occasional external complaints.
A case register exists in the {HELPDESK}, but correspondence and meeting records remain separate.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Evidence collection uses case identifiers and authorised links; uncertain matches require review.
Consent and access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which service records have reliable case identifiers and usable interfaces?
What commitments can the manager make without further approval?
How much time currently goes into preparation, meetings, and follow-up?
Which complaint categories require restricted access or a separate escalation route?
Which national consultation requirements and internal agreements apply?
research_questions: Does existing {HELPDESK} configuration already cover action tracking and reminders?
Can a representative sample of briefs be checked reliably against linked evidence?
Does draft review save time when complaints contain conflicting accounts?
new_work: Review suggested routing, briefs, and meeting records.
Resolve missing identifiers, inaccessible evidence, and conflicting accounts.
Maintain the service directory, reminder rules, and connector permissions.
Check that sensitive complaint details do not enter wider meeting records.

tasks.short: Supervise administrative staff, organise daily work, and orient and train new starters.

steps.what: Review service queues, staff availability, and outstanding work.
Assign priorities and responsibilities, considering skills, workload, and individual circumstances.
Observe work, coach staff, resolve difficulties, and give feedback.
Check each starter's role, start date, and required induction activities.
Assemble role instructions, induction materials, and practice examples.
Welcome starters, demonstrate procedures, and check understanding through supervised practice.
Check training completions and remind staff about outstanding activities.
Record agreed development needs and support actions for later check-ins.

loop.input: Manager-entered coaching notes, practice observations, and agreed support actions.
loop.output: Draft factual development record without scores or inferred personal traits.
loop.check: Manager checks every statement against notes and confirms the agreed actions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; ambiguous observations return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative notes need concise wording; structured support actions use templates directly.

tasks.design: Create a permission-controlled workload view from the {HELPDESK}, {PROJECT}, and availability fields in the {HCM}; managers continue assigning work. Configure role-based starter checklists, approved induction packs, and completion reminders across the {HCM}, {DOCS}, {LMS}, and {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop drafts development records from manager-entered notes for approval before filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Starter data, procedures, and training records have separate owners. Human supervision was often treated as one indivisible activity, leaving its supporting paperwork unchanged.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration can assemble approved materials and trigger checklists. AI-assisted coding makes modest integrations easier to build, while bounded drafting can reduce some note-writing effort.
tasks.still_hard: Coaching, fair allocation, and judging readiness remain personal responsibilities. GDPR and national employment rules govern staff records; any expansion into AI allocation or performance evaluation needs a separate EU AI Act assessment and applicable employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice uncertainty, build confidence, adapt teaching, and distinguish a training gap from workload or personal difficulties.

ambition.what: Short practice clinics for rare administrative exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling induction materials and tracking completions, leaving more time for observation and coaching. Existing staffing and employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Balance service capacity and coordinate changes across administrative teams.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, dependency management, and transparent prioritisation.

reach.task: Identify essential administrative services and arrange backup coverage.
reach.learn: Service dependency mapping, recovery priorities, and practical continuity exercises.

evidence.claim: Role-based induction checklists, approved document assembly, and completion reminders can use existing configuration.
The digest supplies no directly matched case establishing savings for administrative staff supervision.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions and safeguards.
Certain AI systems for worker allocation, monitoring, or performance evaluation fall within Annex III; routine induction checklists alone do not establish that classification.
Where workplace high-risk AI is deployed, Article 26 includes advance information duties toward affected workers and their representatives.

assumptions: The manager supervises a small administrative team and personally handles part of starter orientation.
Approved role profiles, induction materials, and training completion records exist.
The workload view uses availability, not absence reasons or inferred productivity scores.
Induction packs select approved content without generating new procedures.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Consent and access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; elapsed consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Which induction features are already configured in the {HCM} and {LMS}?
Are procedures current, approved, and mapped to roles?
Can service queues be linked without exposing confidential staff information?
Who may access development records, and how long are they retained?
Which national consultation requirements and collective agreements apply?
How much orientation is delivered by the manager rather than a colleague?
research_questions: Can starter checklists and document assembly be configured without custom code?
Does the combined workload view improve allocation discussions without individual scoring?
Does reviewing drafted development notes take less time than entering structured notes directly?
new_work: Maintain role-to-checklist mappings and approved training materials.
Resolve missing starter data and incorrect completion records.
Review drafted development records and handle staff corrections.
Maintain access controls, retention settings, and integration health.
Design practice clinics from recurring questions and observed training gaps.

role.altitude: The role remains centred on representation, fair supervision, and practical service decisions. Less preparation and tracking work creates room for service improvement and deeper coaching; additional authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Management analysis through recurring complaint causes and service improvement experiments.
Project coordination through capacity planning and cross-team dependencies.
Business continuity through backup coverage for essential administrative services.
skills_to_grow: Configure case ownership, checklists, and reminder rules.
Write clear decision records and evidence-based briefs.
Review model drafts against source records.
Apply staff-data access and retention rules.
Coach through supervised practice and constructive feedback.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small administrative service improvement programme that combines complaint learning, staff practice clinics, and backup coverage, with an agreed budget and escalation mandate.
